implementation_findings.boundary: Atomic current-idle removal and future-idle flag
implementation_findings.finding: The original pool mutex serializes close_future_idle=true with removal of current unique H1 idle entries. Waiter queues remain intact. PoolInner::put offers a usable returned value to waiters before applying future-idle rejection to the unused remainder. A newly created checkout resets the flag once; polling an existing checkout does not reset it. Close is repeatable and nonterminal.

Opted-in unique Pooled leases retain Arc<Mutex<PoolInner>>, the genuine underlying pool. The unchanged sender-readiness/on_idle future retains that lease while the Hyper transport is busy. Its return creates the idle entry or hands off to a waiter. No outer-client timer, response-header count, rebuilt client, or disconnected close marker substitutes for native ownership.

implementation_findings.boundary: Per-entry TTL retention and cancellation races
implementation_findings.finding: Each accepted retained H1 idle insertion takes an actual idle timestamp, unique checked-increment entry ID, cancellation channel and strong pool task guard. Its absolute deadline is that idle timestamp plus the configured timeout. Checkout drops the old cancellation sender, including through IdlePopper partial moves; reinserted values receive fresh IDs and deadlines. Explicit close, global eviction and dead-driver removal drop affected senders. A timeout racing with checkout/reinsertion can remove only its old ID. No-timeout entries wait for cancellation; a configured timeout requires a pool timer. Normal reqwest supplies TokioTimer. These are source findings plus the specified retained tests, not every possible executor/panic schedule.

implementation_findings.boundary: Weak driver liveness and completion races
implementation_findings.finding: The H1 driver retains only a weak pool observer and a connection ID/liveness flag. Observer drop marks liveness false with Release before upgrading/locking the pool, then removes matching idle connection IDs. PoolClient::is_open observes liveness with Acquire; both Pooled::drop and PoolInner::put check it. Thus a driver completed before insertion cannot leave a retained live-looking idle sender. Driver completion racing after a check removes the inserted idle entry; a racing waiter value is checked at receipt and existing retry/error handling remains. Observer cancellation also marks the unavailable driver dead. Early guard release is reviewed in source; no private pool-introspection runtime test is claimed.

The per-host bound rejects excess unused returning values. The global bound counts H1 unique idle entries and evicts the oldest actual idle timestamp, with entry ID as deterministic tie-breaker, across hosts. Eviction cancels only its corresponding expiry task. SDK ordinary construction opts into 2 per host and 100 globally; library defaults remain unlimited unless configured.

Reqwest retains an actual HyperClient clone before its existing retry/cookie/redirect/decompression service layering, and close delegates into that pool. TLS, connector, request, response, body, retry, redirect, decompression and error-module files remain original bytes. The original H1 with_upgrades driver and readiness/error oneshot handling remain; only completion observation is added. Retirement of a pool sender and physical peer shutdown are separate. Optional H2 sharing remains outside this approval.

source_findings: HttpTransport::build configures genuine retained pool ownership, per-host 2/global 100, and inherits normal reqwest 90-second idle timeout. HttpTransport::from_client preserves a normal caller-configured native client boundary.

Client::close_idle_connections forwards only when owns_transport=true. Injected try_with_transport/with_transport and verified try_from_credentials remain caller-owned; positive SDK pacing does not override ownership. Explicit with_owned_transport is a Rust ownership-transfer extension.

new_owned validates trimmed blank access before native transport configuration and maps fallible anonymous cursor construction. Legacy Rust new/with_transport remain permissive and are not relabeled as the Go New mapping.

AccountService selects verified credential construction without anonymous cursor entropy. Execution teardown invokes the ownership-aware SDK hook, preserving its ordinary injected caller-owned no-op route.

retained_evidence.physical_shutdown_observer: The current helper wraps the raw TCP reader below TLS. It records remote EOF/ECONNRESET only, once per connection, excludes test-owned cleanup, and drains bounded remaining raw bytes before normal local close when necessary. TLS close_notify alone, SDK completion and handler completion do not count as physical shutdown.

limitations: The unchanged Hyper sender-readiness path can become ready after the final response frame is buffered but before the resource caller consumes it. Withheld-body schedules establish busy transport behavior, not every buffered-but-unconsumed Go bodyEOFSignal timing or future body-lease semantics.
Go explicit fallible Body.Close and its close_success result have no corresponding current ResourceBody API. The early-close Go row remains unmapped; Rust future/body drop is not claimed equivalent.

Current ordinary SDK request/resource APIs lack caller Context. The three H1 cancellation rows, the retained Login ownership slice and non-nil caller-Context runtime slice are not mapped by this activation; future abort is not a Context-cancellation equivalence claim.

Complete default constructor, OAuth successful/failed Open and owner-drop assembly, all input/provider combinations and failure/error-order paths are not established by custom-client SDK schedules. Actual-pool retention is implemented in the dependency core; public failed Open parity is not inferred.

No private Go PutIdleConn callback/acceptance/error-string or raw pointer identity is compared. Public SDK EOF completion alone does not prove asynchronous pool insertion; actual reuse is measured by subsequent connection IDs.
No HTTP/2/relay activation, admission/TTL/driver retirement, multiplex, uploads, unfinished HEAD, or previously denied supplemental probe is executed or approved by this review.

No native Windows/Darwin, other OS/architecture, distribution/license-union packaging, or final migration verification is inferred. Imported ordinary license texts are intact, but complete workspace release packaging remains a separate obligation.

Arbitrary future Drop/panic/IO/executor/concurrency schedules, private early dead-driver retention release, default native diagnostics/Accept and the unchanged full Rust gate remain bounded/open as documented.
